welcome.title: Welcome to LucidSSH
welcome.subtitle: A simple SSH client for managing servers. Add your first server to connect and start working in the terminal.
welcome.footer: LucidSSH v{{version}} · All data is stored locally on your computer

navigation.title: Navigation
items: Click a path segment at the top — a cd command is inserted automatically
Drag a server from the list onto the tab bar — a new session opens

security.title: Security
items: Before rm -rf, kill -9 and similar, a confirmation appears: type the object name
If the server fingerprint changes — a warning before connecting

tools.title: Tools
items: On errors, a panel slides up with an explanation and “what to check” steps
History keeps commands with filters and notes; passwords and tokens are masked
The button to the right of the input opens the command catalog by category

terminal.title: Terminal
items: A root session is highlighted in red in the path bar
Settings → Terminal lets you type commands directly in the output area

empty.title: No active session
empty.description: Select a server on the left to connect.

fp.bodyFirst: Make sure the fingerprint matches what your hosting provider shows.
fp.explain: A fingerprint is the server's digital thumbprint. It confirms you are connecting to your own server.
fp.bodyChanged: The saved fingerprint of “{{host}}” does not match the new one. This happens after a server reinstall or update, but may also mean a man-in-the-middle attack. Verify the new fingerprint via an independent source: hosting panel or server console.
fp.ackChanged: I verified the new fingerprint via an independent source

explain.rm-recursive: This command deletes “{{target}}” with all its contents. This action is irreversible.
explain.dd-write: dd will overwrite “{{target}}” — all data on it will be lost beyond recovery.
explain.mkfs: mkfs will create a new filesystem on “{{target}}”, erasing all data on the device.
explain.chmod-777: chmod -R 777 makes “{{target}}” and everything inside readable and writable by everyone — a serious security hole.
explain.truncate: truncate will empty the file “{{target}}”, erasing its contents.
explain.redirect-device: Writing directly to device “{{target}}” will corrupt its filesystem.
explain.shred: shred overwrites “{{target}}” repeatedly, making the data unrecoverable.
explain.wipefs: wipefs erases the filesystem signatures on “{{target}}” — the device becomes unreadable.
explain.fork-bomb: This is a fork bomb: it spawns processes exponentially and freezes the server.
explain.drop-database: This command irreversibly drops the database or table “{{target}}”.
explain.kill-init: Signaling process 1 (init/systemd) will crash the whole system.
explain.generic: This command is recognized as potentially destructive. Review it before running.

snippet.dangerWarn: Dangerous command — it will go to the “Dangerous” section and require confirmation to run
snippet.scopeHint: “For this server” — visible only on this connection. “Global” — available everywhere.

terminal.bellDesc: Play a bell on \a in the output.
terminal.brightBoldDesc: Render bold in a brighter shade.
terminal.selectCopyDesc: Selected text goes straight to the clipboard.
terminal.rightPasteDesc: Paste from the clipboard on right click.
terminal.inlineInputDesc: Type the command in the output line, like a regular terminal. The bottom input is hidden.
terminal.inlineInputGuardWarn: In this mode the Guard does not check commands typed directly in the console. Dangerous-command protection only applies to the bottom input line.

connection.keepaliveDesc: How often to send a keepalive so the connection stays up.
connection.timeoutDesc: How long to wait for the server when connecting.
connection.autoreconnectDesc: Try to restore the connection when it drops.

security.guardDesc: Asks for confirmation before rm -rf, kill -9 and similar, requiring the object name. Turning it off removes all warnings.
security.historyDesc: Store executed commands. Passwords and tokens are always masked. Turning it off stops recording.

interface.expertDesc: Turns off all learning hints at once. Bring them back individually with the toggles below.
interface.hintCatalogDesc: Tips above the input and descriptions in the catalog.
interface.hintTooltipsDesc: Explanatory tooltips on hovering the output.
interface.hintErrorDesc: Pop-up “what to check” panel on errors.
interface.hintConnectDesc: Learning notes in the new connection form.
interface.systemToastsDesc: Toasts on connection loss and long commands finishing when the window is not focused.
interface.longCommandDesc: Notify about commands longer than N seconds. 0 disables it.

about.tagline: A simple SSH client for Windows. Fully local: no account, cloud or telemetry.
about.resetDesc: Restore settings to defaults. Does not touch servers, keys or command history.

notif.disconnect: Connection lost. Click to return and reconnect.
